## Introduction

Hierarchical extension of BWQS [@colicino2020bwqs] where each group (e.g. cohort) has its own
intercept and its own mixture effect, with partial pooling [@gelman2013bda]. The model
`hbwqs` is in `src/models.jl`.

## Setup

The analysis runs in Julia [@bezanson2017julia]; `ExposomicsJulia` provides the shared helpers and models, together with DataFrames.jl [@bouchetvalat2023dataframes] and Turing.jl [@ge2018turing].

```{julia}
#| label: setup
using ExposomicsJulia
using DataFrames, CSV, HTTP, Statistics
using Turing, ReverseDiff
DATA = joinpath(pkgdir(ExposomicsJulia), ".data")
```

## Toy multilevel example

Example dataset from <https://storopoli.io/Bayesian-Julia/pages/11_multilevel_models/>:

* `cheese`: type of cheese from A to D
* `rater`: id of the rater from 1 to 10
* `background`: type of rater, either rural or urban
* `y`: rating of the cheese

```{julia}
#| label: toy-multilevel-example
url = "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/storopoli/Bayesian-Julia/master/datasets/cheese.csv"
cheese = CSV.read(HTTP.get(url).body, DataFrame)

for c in unique(cheese[:, :cheese])
    cheese[:, "cheese_$c"] = ifelse.(cheese[:, :cheese] .== c, 1, 0)
end
cheese[:, :background_int] = map(b -> b == "rural" ? 1 : b == "urban" ? 2 : missing, cheese[:, :background])
first(cheese, 5)
```

```{julia}
#| label: toy-multilevel-example-2
X   = Matrix(select(cheese, Between(:cheese_A, :cheese_D)));
y   = cheese[:, :y];
idx = cheese[:, :background_int];
```

## Exposure mixture by cohort

`.data/bwqs_tmp.csv`: quantised urinary metals
`UAs_q … UPb_q`, covariates in columns 8–12 and 15–17, cohort index.

```{julia}
#| label: exposure-mixture-by-cohort
#| eval: false
DT  = CSV.read(joinpath(DATA, "bwqs_tmp.csv"), DataFrame)
M   = Matrix(select(DT, Between(:UAs_q, :UPb_q)));
X   = Matrix(DT[:, vcat(8:12, 15:17)]);
y   = DT[:, :y];
idx = DT[:, :cohort];

model_h = hbwqs(M, X, idx, y)
chain_h = sample(model_h, NUTS(; adtype = AutoReverseDiff(; compile = true)), 1000)
chain_summary(chain_h; pattern = "w[")
```
